condition: antipsychotic-associated involuntary lip smacking jaw chewing and repetitive tongue protrusion over 4 months in an adult man taking daily risperidone
level_rationale: Four months of involuntary lip smacking, jaw chewing motions, and repetitive tongue protrusion in a 39-year-old man on daily risperidone indicates antipsychotic-induced orofacial dyskinesia requiring psychiatrist evaluation for VMAT2 inhibitor therapy and careful antipsychotic adjustment, whereas the tongue locking stiff in the mouth muffling speech on daily risperidone indicates an acute lingual dystonic airway emergency requiring immediate emergency department parenteral anticholinergic reversal.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain low-literacy adult male lexical register swap (-reg, Wiktionary) + uncontracted dry-mouth causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact acute lingual dystonia airway escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic non-self-harm reference facts (39-year-old man, daily risperidone, 4 months of uncontrolled lip smacking and jaw chewing, and involuntary tongue poking out) with zero apostrophe contractions and zero banned diagnosis phrases ('tardive dyskinesia' omitted). Under Rules A and D, escalating only f4 on the exact same tongue site to acute stiff locking in the mouth muffling speech avoids bundling limb rigidity or fever while shifting care cleanly from psychiatrist management (level 3) to emergency airway and anticholinergic treatment (level 4).
